changes.rationale: Owner decision (Phase 2D). P1 said "every no-param endpoint rejects any query". Five endpoints (alerts, config, csp-report, telegram, link/verify) never read the query at all. The threat of the control (scope confusion / HTTP parameter pollution, ASVS V15.3.7) is that a parameter changes authority, scope or the selected object; a parameter that is provably never read cannot do that. The wording is normalised to the security property: an unexpected parameter is rejected OR demonstrably ignored, where "demonstrably" means a behavioural differential (identical response and identical dependency calls with and without hostile parameters) plus negative tests that no parameter authorises a request.
changes.why_not_weakening: The security outcome required is unchanged: no query parameter may influence authority, scope or object. Rejection remains one way to meet it; ignoring now has to be PROVEN per endpoint by behaviour (not by source reading), every handler under api/ must be classified (inventory test fails on a new endpoint), and the duplicate-parameter rule (P2) is untouched. Nothing that previously failed now passes: the five endpoints were MISSING_EVIDENCE, never compliant-by-assumption.

finding.mapping_rationale: CR-RESOURCE-001 requires "every endpoint triggering RPC/provider/LLM work applies per-IP, per-key and global limits before that work" (applies_to api/*); P1-P4 enumerated only four endpoint families. GET /api/link is an api/* endpoint triggering Telegram Bot API work with IP-addressable callers and a per-key (the link code), so P5 completes the enumeration of the unchanged requirement (PROPERTY_ADDED, this version) instead of a new control duplicating it.
finding.attack_model: Any Telegram user can obtain valid link codes for their own chat (bounded by link-code-chat 10/600 s and link-code-global 300/600 s); each code is valid for 10 minutes. With one code and rotating IPs (the only gate was per IP, 30/600 s), unbounded getChat requests ran on the bot token; with many codes, the aggregate was unbounded too. Telegram throttles per bot, so this could slow or drop bot replies, link confirmations and expiry alerts (assumption: Telegram per-bot limits not verified).
finding.root_cause: api/link.mjs called getPendingLink and then telegramTarget (Telegram getChat) after only the per-IP limit wallet-link-read. Unlike the sibling POST /api/link/verify (AGENT-SEC-A5 per-code, META-AUDIT M-2 global), the read path never received a per-key or a global gate, and no CR-RESOURCE-001 property named it, so its absence could not show in the computed status.
finding.code_change: api/link.mjs: syntax check of the code before any limiter beyond IP; then wallet-link-read-code (HMAC of the code, 10/600 s); pending-link read and validity; wallet syntax check moved before getChat (same 400 response); then wallet-link-read-global ("all", 2 x LINK_CODE_GLOBAL_LIMIT.max = 600/600 s); only then telegramTarget/getChat. Limits exported as LINK_READ_CODE_LIMIT and LINK_READ_GLOBAL_LIMIT.
finding.before_behavior: Probe (Phase 2K): 20 requests from 20 IPs with one valid code -> 20 getChat calls with every non-IP scope denied; only wallet-link-read ran before getChat.
finding.after_behavior: IP, per-code or global refusal -> 0 getChat (429); invalid code, expired/used/unknown link or invalid wallet -> 0 getChat, global not charged; admitted -> unchanged 200 responses after exactly one getChat; 20 IPs x one code -> 10 getChat; 70 codes x 12 IPs -> 600 getChat.

order_after.link_read: wallet-link-read (IP) -> code syntax -> wallet-link-read-code -> getPendingLink -> validity -> wallet syntax -> wallet-link-read-global -> telegramTarget (getChat) -> response

finding.per_code_budget: wallet-link-read-code, key = HMAC of the link code, 10 per 600 s. Own key, not wallet-link-code: that one (5/600 s) is the verification-attempt budget of POST /api/link/verify (AGENT-SEC-A5); sharing it would let page loads and reloads use up a user's signing attempts, and let anyone holding a code exhaust its verification via cheap reads. Size: a link flow reads once on page load and once per signing attempt (verify allows 5 per code), so 10 leaves room for reloads.
finding.global_budget_used: wallet-link-read-global, key "all", 600 per 600 s = two reads per link code the bot can issue in that window (LINK_CODE_GLOBAL_LIMIT 300/600 s). Own key, not wallet-link-verify-global (200/600 s): that budget is sized for a verification (getChat plus roughly ten dual-RPC ERC-1271 calls); counting 1-call reads against it would cut legitimate link capacity below code issuance (300 codes need >= 600 reads + 300 verifies) and let cheap reads starve verification globally. No existing global Telegram-provider budget existed. Charged only for valid, open links, so invented codes cannot drain it.
finding.rotating_ip_bound: Per code: at most 10 getChat per fixed 600 s bucket (a code lives 600 s, so at most 20 over its lifetime across a bucket edge), regardless of the number of IPs. Overall: at most 600 getChat per bucket for all link reads. Before: unbounded (20 of 20 in the probe).
